title: Exentra embeds Flowable in its own project-controlling software, making it an OEM rather than a channel
content:
Exentra's Flowable listing describes the engine as embedded in its custom project-controlling software. The research classes the firm as a vendor rather than an integrator on that basis alone.

What the listing therefore records is a build-time dependency inside a product, not a delivery practice serving third parties. That inverts the usual reasoning about tool adoption: where an integrator's platform choice is made per client engagement and can be revisited, an OEM's is a component decision inside a shipping product, owned by whoever owns the roadmap. The relationship a small vendor can hope for is displacement of a component, not attachment to a project.

The record is directory-thin beyond that. Unlike Avaloq, no headcount is recorded, no contact was resolved, and the row was never imprint-swept — it is the Flowable card and the inference drawn from it, mined on 2026-08-18.
